newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa, U.N. officials meet ahead of Zaire talks.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa, U.N. officials meet ahead of Zaire talks.

text.p: South African and U.N. officials met in Pretoria on Thursday to wrap up arrangements for the first meeting between leaders of Zaire's warring factions, a spokesman said.

Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad and the joint U.N. and Organisation of African Unity envoy Mohamed Sahnoun discussed arrangements which were likely to be made public on Friday, the Foreign Ministry spokesman said.

Delegations representing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila, whose forces have seized about a quarter of Zaire since October, are due to meet in South Africa this weekend, possibly from Friday.

Pahad earlier told state radio that South Africa had gained the impression from Kabila, who held preparatory discussions in Pretoria last month, that he was committed to democracy in the Central African country.
"We've always had the feeling from the first proximity talks in South Africa that the rebels were committed to finding a peaceful solution.

"They wanted to be sure the negotiations would not take place over a protracted period...and ultimately they wanted to be sure that any negotiations must have as an objective finding the process that will lead to genuine democracy," Pahad said.
He said the situation in Zaire, which has created another African refugee crisis, demanded that a political solution be found as soon as possible.
"I would hope that while a ceasefire will be an element (in the talks), they will use the opportunity to discuss the modalities for any future, more detailed negotiations," he said.
"A ceasefire must be the first step to finding a possible long-term political solution."

A South African government source said initial preparations were for meetings around Pretoria or Johannesburg, both in the heartlands Gauteng province, but he added that nothing had yet been approved by the delegations.
The team due to represent Mobutu's government was expected to meet in Zaire on Thursday to harmonise views on the agenda of the talks and leave for Pretoria on Friday.
The team, headed by Mobutu's security adviser Honore Ngbanda, includes opposition representatives and supporters of Mobutu, who has ruled since seizing power in 1965.
The rebels, who have vowed to topple Mobutu, want the talks to lead to a meeting between him and Kabila.
U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Wednesday he was hopeful that the Zairean government and the rebels could set a date for a ceasefire during their talks in South Africa.
He said he expected both sides to agree on a date by the end of the week for both proper negotiations and a ceasefire.
"I expect that the parties will agree to a date before the end of this week or not later than April 5," he said, adding that Sahnoun would then open the negotiations.
